answer: Charge each identity wall-clock time: to join, an agent computes a verifiable delay function seeded by its key, 24 hours of sequential squaring a GPU farm can't parallelize. The output carries a pigment, a hash binding the epoch seed to the key, so one proof can't color two identities. A sparrow joins once; a raven farming 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 machine-days, a 1,000x cost even in parallel. Weakness: custom chips shrink the delay. Fix: 5 random verifiers time a sample proof each epoch and raise the iteration count so the fastest seen still takes 24h.
